summary: Dedicated pool experiencing GPU slot fragmentation causing intermittent batching stalls and elevated p99 latency
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:40 UTC, a ClarityAI customer on a Dedicated pool reported repeated p99 latency spikes and a set of requests that appeared to 'hang' in batching for 10–40s. Impact: ~12% of requests in their high-throughput route hit elevated p99s and several timed out, affecting production traffic. Environment: Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-cc-84), prod-us-west, mixed model traffic (gpt-j-6b, llama-2-13b). Observed behavior: - Normal throughput periods interleaved with 5–15 minute windows where batching stalls; internal scheduling logs show many small free slots not usable for new batch allocations (fragmentation). - GPUs report lower utilization during stalls but serve long-lived cached KV pages. - No obvious OOM or kernel crashes; 500s were rare, more commonly long tail latency and batch queue timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs production workload with many mid-sized requests (avg tokens per request ~120) across two models pinned to the dedicated pool.
2) System enters steady-state for ~30–60 minutes.
3) After warmup, SRE observed periodic windows where new requests queue for long durations before being assigned to a GPU batch; existing batches still complete but batch sizes are consistently 1-2 instead of 8-16.
4) Repro rate observed ~3/10 hours in customer workload; not reproduced in synthetic load that uses perfectly balanced slot sizing.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:15 UTC - Initial triage by Support: Confirmed p99 spike windows correlate with high fragmentation_ratio in gpu-monitor metrics.

2026-03-10 11:02 UTC - SRE hypothesis: Fragmentation likely caused by a mix of long-lived KV-cache reservations and uneven slot sizing when tenants submit a mix of short and medium requests; scheduler can't coalesce small free slots into requested batch shapes.

2026-03-10 12:30 UTC - Reproduced partial behavior in a canary by replaying customer trace: when we interleave many 20-token and 120-token requests with sticky KV usage, fragmentation increases and batch sizes collapse to 1-2.
2026-03-10 13:05 UTC - Checked node-level metrics: no GPU OOMs, kernel errors. Observed small but consistent CPU scheduling queuing on the scheduler thread during stalls.
2026-03-11 09:20 UTC - Applied temporary scheduler policy change (allow compaction pass every 5m) and observed immediate improvement in batch sizing for the canary route.
2026-03-12 16:10 UTC - Customer reports reduced p99 after temporary change, but intermittent windows still occur under burst patterns.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC - <Aisha Patel>: Notified SRE and asked for earliest ETA on root cause; provided customer traces and tenant id.
2026-03-10 10:25 UTC - <SRE - Linh Tran>: Confirmed fragmentation spikes in cluster metrics. Investigating scheduler compaction heuristics; will try a non-disruptive compaction pass on canary nodes.
2026-03-10 14:12 UTC - <Marco Ivanov>: Ran a compaction job on 2 nodes; saw batch size recovery and immediate p99 improvement for canary traffic. Scheduling controlled rollout to affected pool.
2026-03-11 11:44 UTC - <Customer - ClarityAI (R. Gomez)>: Thanks — we've seen much better behavior for several hours. Will alert if the pattern reappears. Our peak windows show the highest risk.
2026-03-14 07:22 UTC - <Linh Tran>: Added metric alert for fragmentation_ratio>0.6 and added autoscaler tie-in to trigger compaction action and temporary reservation consolidation.
resolution: Workaround applied: 2026-03-11 08:50 UTC we enabled periodic scheduler compaction and a short reservation consolidation window that temporarily pauses KV cache pinning for low-priority tenants during high fragmentation. We manually evicted one noisy tenant that was retaining many small reservations and moved their heavy background jobs to a different maintenance pool. Result: immediate reduction in fragmentation_ratio (from ~0.67 to ~0.18) and p99 dropped from ~34s to ~1.4s for the affected route. Long-term plan agreed (see follow-up actions).
follow_up_actions: Implement permanent compaction pass in scheduler with safe concurrency limits (engineering ticket created)
Add fragmentation_ratio metric to Console dashboards and create alert with runbook
Tweak autoscaler to consider fragmentation signals and trigger minor consolidation or short-lived reservations instead of full-scale node adds
Document KV cache pinning best-practices for Dedicated customers and provide guidance to ClarityAI to reduce long-lived small reservations
Consider scheduler algorithm improvement: allow splitting/merging of slot allocations to reduce unusable free fragments
Postmortem due 2026-03-20 with actions assigned to SRE and Scheduler team
